newsitem.title: CHINA: China woman thrilled to face deportation from HK.
newsitem.headline: China woman thrilled to face deportation from HK.

text.p: Unlike most illegal immigrants in Hong Kong, Mok Chek-mui from mainland China is thrilled to face deportation, a Hong Kong newspaper reported on Saturday.
Immigration authorities ordered Mok, 38, to leave on Saturday because her temporary visa had expired. But Mok wants to leave anyway -- so she can come back and work legally.

Mok, a mother of three, only learned after her temporary visa had expired recently that she had been granted a coveted one-way permit, which she must pick up in Haifeng in Guangdong province by Sunday, the Hong Kong Standard said.
But when she tried to leave Hong Kong last week, she was barred for overstaying her visa.
"I am very happy because I can go back to China to claim my one-way permit," Mok was quoted in the English-language daily as saying. "Now I can come to Hong Kong without breaking the law."
Mainlanders married to Hong Kong residents can legally move to the territory, but with thousands in the queue, the wait for a permit from Chinese authorities can last more than a decade.
On Friday, the court fined Mok HK$3,000 (US$388) for overstaying, and the Immigration Department told her she would be deported on Saturday as a special case, the Standard said.
